name: Bug Out in 15 Minutes
description: Can you grab everything you need and leave your home in 15 minutes? This drill tests your bug-out readiness from a cold start.
steps: Grab your bug-out bag from its stored location
Check bag has water — minimum 2 litres per person
Check bag has food — minimum 3 days supply
Grab any prescription medications
Grab ID documents and cash
Check your power bank is charged and in the bag
Grab your radio if you have one
Tell every household member the rally point
Lock the house
Be at your designated meeting point

name: Blackout Response
description: The power just went out. Can your household transition to off-grid living in under 5 minutes? This drill tests your immediate response.
steps: Locate your primary torch without using your phone screen
Get backup lighting on in the main living area
Check your power bank — is it charged above 80%?
Turn fridge and freezer to maximum cold to slow spoilage
Check your water storage — how many days do you have?
Turn on your battery radio and find a news frequency
Confirm everyone in the household knows where candles and torches are
Note the time the power went out
Identify what heating you have if this lasts overnight
Check on any vulnerable neighbours

name: Radio Check
description: Normal comms are down. Can you get on air and make contact within 10 minutes from a cold start?
steps: Locate your primary radio
Connect or check antenna
Power on — confirm battery level above 50%
Tune to your primary frequency (check Radio Notebook if needed)
Listen for 60 seconds — any traffic on frequency?
Make a call on your primary frequency
Log the attempt — time, frequency, result
If no response — switch to backup frequency and repeat
Try your local repeater
If all radio fails — note it and move to mesh or CB backup plan

name: Bleeding Control
description: Practice drill only. You will need a bandage or cloth and a rolled towel to simulate a limb. Do NOT practise on a real wound. Target: pressure applied within 30 seconds.
steps: Identify the bleed location (simulated on rolled towel)
Apply direct pressure immediately with cloth or dressing
Maintain firm continuous pressure — do not lift to check
After 3 minutes — has bleeding (simulation) slowed?
If not controlled — pack the wound tightly with gauze
If limb bleed not controlled after packing — apply tourniquet
Note the time tourniquet applied — write it on the skin
Keep patient warm and lying down
Call 112 or send for help
Keep talking to the patient — monitor consciousness

name: Family Comms Plan Test
description: Does every member of your household know the emergency plan without being told? Run this unannounced if possible.
steps: Ask each family member: what is our rally point if we cannot go home?
Ask each family member: what is the out-of-area contact number?
Ask each family member: where is the bug-out bag?
Ask each family member: where is the first aid kit?
Ask each family member: where are the torches?
Ask each family member: what do we do if the power goes out overnight?
Ask each family member: what is our meeting point if we get separated?
Does every member have ICE contacts in their phone?
Does every member know to text not call in an emergency?
Does every member know the European emergency number is 112?

name: Water Supply Check
description: How long can your household survive on water alone if the mains goes off right now? This drill audits your water supply and purification capability.
steps: Locate all stored water in the house — count litres
Check expiry or fill dates on stored water containers
Calculate days of water at 2L per adult per day
Locate your water purification method (tablets, filter, or boiling setup)
Test your purification method — run water through it
Identify your nearest natural water source
Check you have containers to collect and transport water
Check you have fuel or means to boil water if needed
Update your stockpile app with current water levels
If under 7 days supply — plan to increase storage this week

name: Full Comms Blackout
description: Mobile networks, internet, and landlines are all down. Can you communicate with your network using alternative methods only?
steps: Switch your phone to aeroplane mode — simulate no mobile network
Get your primary radio on air
Attempt contact on your primary net frequency
Attempt contact via your local repeater
Check your MeshCore or Meshtastic device if you have one
Attempt contact via CB radio if you have one
Leave a voice message on your primary frequency for your net
Identify who in your network you were unable to reach
Note all frequencies and methods attempted in your Radio Notebook
Establish a plan for next attempt time and frequency

name: Vehicle Readiness Check
description: If you needed to leave right now, is your vehicle ready? This drill checks your vehicle is prepped for an emergency evacuation.
steps: Check fuel level — is it above half a tank?
Check tyre pressures including spare
Locate your vehicle emergency kit — torch, hi-vis, jump leads
Check you have a paper map of your area in the vehicle
Check first aid kit is in the vehicle and stocked
Check you have water and food in the vehicle (minimum 24hrs)
Check your radio or scanner is in the vehicle and working
Identify your primary bug-out route
Identify your backup bug-out route if primary is blocked
Confirm all household members know the vehicle rally point
